The drawing shows a purine core with three substituents.

**Purine core.** The six-membered ring has C6 at the top, bearing the morpholine. Going around the ring from C6: N1 on the right, C2 at the lower right (bearing the benzimidazole), N3 at the bottom, C4 on the left (ring fusion), and C5 at the upper left (ring fusion).

**Five-membered ring.** C5 is bonded to N7 (drawn as "N" at the upper left), which is double-bonded to C8. C8 is bonded to N9, which carries the methyl group. N9 is bonded to C4.

**Substituents.**
- C6 carries a morpholine attached through its nitrogen: N1CCOCC1.
- C2 carries a benzimidazol-1-yl group attached through N1. Its C2 position bears an isopropyl group, and the benzo ring is fused on the other side.

**SMILES construction.**
- Start with the methylated N9: Cn1cnc2c1nc(nc2N1CCOCC1)...
- Check the ring connectivity. The string Cn1cnc2c1nc(...)nc2N3CCOCC3 reads as N9(Me), C8, N7, C5 (opens ring 2), C4 (closes ring 1 to N9), N3, C2, N1, C6 (closes ring 2 to C5). This matches the drawing.
- Add the benzimidazole at C2: -n4c(C(C)C)nc5ccccc45.

Full SMILES: Cn1cnc2c1nc(nc2N1CCOCC1)-n1c(C(C)C)nc2ccccc21

SMILES: Cn1cnc2c1nc(nc2N1CCOCC1)-n1c(C(C)C)nc2ccccc21
